newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends sharply up, backwardation eases.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends sharply up, backwardation eases.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures closed sharply higher on Monday with gains inspired by the strong performance of NYMEX heating oil, brokers said.
January gas oil ended up $4.50 a tonne at $232, although February fared better gaining $5.75 on the day. The front month backwardation shed $1.25 on the day to close at $3.25 a tonne.
"The whole market has come up because heating oil has been very strong this afternoon," said one broker. "But a lot of the volume going through has been on the spread."
The Jan/Feb spread touched a low of +$2.75 a tonne.
The spread came under pressure as dealers rolled forward long positions ahead of the January contract's expiry on Friday.
Cold weather was still the main driver behind the markets on both sides of the Atlantic, brokers said.

Independent weather forecaster Weather Services Corp said European temperatures would remain below normal until Thursday, while in the U.S. Northeast temperatures would dip below normal after a mild spell.
February Brent also surged higher, trading 54 cents up at $24.66 a barrel at 1802 GMT, just off a session high of $24.70.
"It's all heat led," said a broker.
